title: Beyond prediction: explainable machine learning for ferritin estimation from complete blood count.
summary: In 12,450 adult laboratory records, five supervised models estimated low ferritin from complete blood count and demographic features. On the balanced 7,200-sample dataset, the artificial neural network had the best low-ferritin classification result (AUC 0.837; F1 0.760); regression had global R² 0.32, with stronger performance in lower ferritin ranges. The evaluation used one laboratory source and does not establish external screening validity.
ai_technology: Five supervised models, including logistic regression, XGBoost and an artificial neural network, classified ferritin below 30 ng/mL and also estimated continuous ferritin from CBC and demographic features; SHAP summarized feature contributions.
organization: Ankara Etlik City Hospital; Ankara University

evidence.tested: The primary abstract and Results report analysis of 12,450 adult laboratory records, a balanced 7,200-sample dataset, five supervised algorithms, ANN low-ferritin classification AUC 0.837 and F1 0.760, and regression global R² 0.32. The input review notes cross-validation and held-out testing, with single-source records and moderate regression fit limiting screening interpretation.
evidence.unknown: All records came from a single laboratory source; no independent external validation or clinically validated screening use is established, and continuous ferritin regression had global R² 0.32.
evidence.ai_role: Five supervised models, including logistic regression, XGBoost and an artificial neural network, classified ferritin below 30 ng/mL and also estimated continuous ferritin from CBC and demographic features; SHAP summarized feature contributions.
